claim: The Legislature convenes every year; the constitutional date may be changed by law
quote: The legislature shall convene in regular session each year on the fourth Monday in January, but the month and day may be changed by law.

claim: A regular session may last no more than 120 days, extendable once by 10 days
quote: The legislature shall adjourn from regular session no later than one hundred twenty consecutive calendar days from the date it convenes

claim: By statute the Legislature convenes on the third Tuesday in January
quote: The legislature shall convene at the capital each year on the third Tuesday in January at 1:00 p.m.

claim: By statute a regular session must adjourn within 90 days
quote: The legislature shall adjourn from a regular session within 90 consecutive calendar days

claim: During session a bill becomes law if not acted on within 15 days, Sundays excepted
quote: while the legislature is in session, the governor neither signs nor vetoes it within fifteen days, Sundays excepted, after its delivery to him

claim: Out of session the governor has 20 days, Sundays excepted, after delivery
quote: If the legislature is not in session and the governor neither signs nor vetoes a bill within twenty days, Sundays excepted, after its delivery to him, the bill becomes law.

claim: Laws take effect ninety days after enactment unless two-thirds of each house set another date
quote: Laws passed by the legislature become effective ninety days after enactment.

claim: Acts become effective 90 days after becoming law unless two-thirds provide otherwise
quote: Acts become effective 90 days after becoming law

claim: All local government powers are vested in boroughs and cities
quote: All local government powers shall be vested in boroughs and cities.

claim: The entire state is divided into boroughs, organized or unorganized
quote: The entire State shall be divided into boroughs, organized or unorganized.

claim: Areas outside organized boroughs form a single unorganized borough
quote: Areas of the state that are not within the boundaries of an organized borough constitute a single unorganized borough.

claim: The Legislature provides services in the unorganized borough
quote: The legislature shall provide for the performance of services it deems necessary or advisable in unorganized boroughs

claim: An organized borough's governing body is the assembly
quote: The governing body of the organized borough shall be the assembly

claim: Cities are part of the borough in which they are located
quote: shall be a part of the borough in which they are located

claim: A city's governing body is the council
quote: The governing body of a city shall be the council.

claim: Voters of a first class borough or city may adopt a home rule charter
quote: The qualified voters of any borough of the first class or city of the first class may adopt, amend, or repeal a home rule charter

claim: A home rule borough or city may exercise all legislative powers not prohibited by law or charter
quote: A home rule borough or city may exercise all legislative powers not prohibited by law or by charter.

claim: A home rule municipality is a chartered city or borough or a unified municipality
quote: It is a city or a borough that has adopted a home rule charter, or it is a unified municipality.

claim: General law municipalities are first, second and third class boroughs and first and second class cities
quote: General law municipalities are of five classes: (1) first class boroughs; (2) second class boroughs; (3) third class boroughs; (4) first class cities; (5) second class cities.

claim: No area may newly incorporate as a third class borough
quote: An area may not incorporate as a third class borough.

claim: A first class or home rule city needs at least 400 permanent residents to incorporate
quote: the community has 400 or more permanent residents

claim: A community meeting all other standards may incorporate as a second class city
quote: may incorporate as a second class city

claim: Cities may be reclassified between first and second class by petition and vote
quote: A second class city may be reclassified as a first class city.

claim: A general law borough or first class city may adopt a charter
quote: A general law borough or first class city may adopt a charter for its own government.

claim: Only listed provisions of Title 29 bind home rule municipalities
quote: Only the following provisions of this title apply to home rule municipalities as prohibitions on acting otherwise than as provided.

claim: Borough legislative power is in the assembly; city legislative power in the council
quote: The legislative power of a borough is vested in the assembly. The legislative power of a city is vested in the council.

claim: Assembly composition is set by the incorporation petition, charter or ordinance
quote: prescribed by charter or ordinance

claim: A first class city council has six members and a second class city council seven, at large unless changed by ordinance
quote: Each first class city has a council of six members elected by the voters at large. Each second class city has a council of seven members elected by the voters at large.

claim: Governing body members serve three-year terms unless a charter or ordinance sets up to four
quote: A member of the governing body is elected for a three-year term and until a successor qualifies, unless a different term not exceeding four years is prescribed by home rule charter or ordinance.

claim: The mayor of a borough or first class city is elected at large for three years unless an ordinance sets up to four
quote: The mayor of a borough or first class city is elected at large. The mayor of a borough or first class city serves a term of three years, unless by ordinance a different term not to exceed four years is provided.

claim: A second class city's mayor is chosen by and from the council
quote: The mayor of a second class city is elected by and from the council

claim: A second class city may have voters elect the mayor from the council
quote: a second class city may by ordinance provide that the mayor is elected, from the council, by the voters rather than by the council

claim: Without a manager plan the mayor is chief administrator
quote: If a municipality has not adopted a manager plan of government, the mayor is the chief administrator

claim: The regular municipal election is the first Tuesday of October each year unless an ordinance sets another date or interval
quote: The date of a regular election is the first Tuesday of October annually, unless a different date or interval of years is provided by ordinance.

claim: Each municipality sets its own election rules
quote: The governing body shall prescribe the rules for conducting an election.

claim: Municipal candidates are nominated by declaration or petition set by ordinance
quote: the governing body shall provide by ordinance for nominations of elected officials by providing for declaration of candidacy or for petition requiring the signatures of not more than 10 voters, or for both

claim: Unless an ordinance says otherwise, a runoff is held if no candidate gets over 40 percent
quote: Unless otherwise provided by ordinance, a runoff election shall be held if no candidate receives over 40 percent of the votes cast for the office of (1) mayor; or (2) member of the governing body or school board if candidates run for a designated seat.

claim: The runoff is between the top two and within three weeks after certification
quote: The runoff election shall be between the two candidates receiving the greatest number of votes for the seat.

claim: Municipal voters must be state-qualified, registered and 30-day residents
quote: has been a resident of the municipality for 30 days immediately preceding the election

claim: The state general election is in November of even-numbered years
quote: The general election is held on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November in every even numbered year.

claim: The state primary is the third Tuesday in August of even-numbered years
quote: The primary election is held on the third Tuesday in August of every even-numbered year.

claim: The state primary is a top-four nonpartisan open primary for state executive and legislative offices
quote: may cast a vote for any candidate for each elective state executive and state and national legislative office, without limitations based on the political party or political group affiliation of either the voter or the candidate

claim: The state primary only narrows the field to four; it does not choose party nominees
quote: The primary election does not serve to determine the nominee of a political party or political group but serves only to narrow the number of candidates whose names will appear on the ballot at the general election.

claim: State general elections use ranked-choice voting
quote: All general elections shall be conducted by ranked-choice voting.

claim: Each organized borough is a borough school district; home rule and first class cities in the unorganized borough are city districts; the rest are REAAs
quote: each home rule and first class city in the unorganized borough is a city school district; (2) each organized borough is a borough school district; (3) the area outside organized boroughs and outside home rule and first class cities is divided into regional educational attendance areas

claim: Districts of 5,000 students or fewer have five-member boards (seven by ordinance)
quote: has a school board of five members

claim: Larger districts have boards of seven, nine or eleven
quote: has a school board of seven, nine, or eleven members, as established by ordinance

claim: Municipal school board members are elected at the regular election for three-year terms, at large unless voters approve otherwise
quote: members of a school board are elected at the regular election for three-year terms and until their successors take office. Members are elected at large unless a different method of election has been approved by the voters in a regular election.

claim: In a third class borough the assembly is the school board
quote: The assembly is the school board for a third class borough.

claim: A regional educational attendance area is run by an elected regional school board of 5 to 11 members
quote: shall elect a regional school board of not less than five nor more than eleven members

claim: Regional school board elections are held annually on the first Tuesday in October, supervised by the state
quote: elections shall be held annually on the first Tuesday in October. Elections shall be supervised by the director of elections in the office of the lieutenant governor

claim: A regional school board may opt out of runoff requirements
quote: if a school board by resolution so requests
